domain: Religious Studies / Halakhic Authority / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of rabbinic preservation of Temple sacrifice law (Kodashim) through continuous study for ~1,900 years without performance. The kernel is the commitment to Temple sacrifice as a binding obligation. Two readings contest whether study-without-performance constitutes genuine occupation of the commitment or merely symbolic archiving. This is a D1/D4 boundary case: is the commitment functioning (study as legitimate substitute) or absent (study as memorial for a dead practice)?

key_entities: Kodashim (Talmudic order on Temple sacrifice law)
Rabbinic authority structure (post-70 CE interpretive tradition)
Temple (destroyed 70 CE, physical site of sacrifice performance)
Study practice (continuous textual engagement without performance)
key_tensions: Study as occupation vs study as archiving (is the commitment alive or symbolically preserved?)
Halakhic continuity vs performance impossibility (binding law with no execution pathway)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Temple sacrifice as divinely mandated obligation binding on the Jewish people
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Rabbinic interpretive tradition claiming continuity from Sinaitic revelation through oral law transmission

readings.expected_structural_delta: Low extractiveness — study is the constraint's current form; no victim set (obligation fulfilled through study); authority structure absorbs impossibility of performance without surfacing revision need

readings.authority_grounding: Performance-only interpretation — obligation remains unfulfilled, study is memorial/preparation
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate extractiveness — entire post-Temple period is non-compliance; victim set is the unfulfilled divine command; authority structure maintains binding status of unperformable law

readings.commitment: Obligation is suspended (not fulfilled, not violated) pending messianic restoration
readings.authority_grounding: Eschatological reading — current era is interregnum where obligation neither binds nor lapses
readings.expected_structural_delta: Very low extractiveness — no current obligation, no victim set; authority structure defers adjudication to future restoration event; study is neither compliance nor preparation but maintenance of knowledge-in-waiting

omegas.description: Is this D1 (functioning — study is legitimate revision-substitute) or D4 (absent — study is memorial for dead practice)? The study-as-occupation reading treats it as D1; study-as-archiving treats it as D4. The boundary collapses if 'study equals performance' is itself a revision that the authority structure cannot acknowledge as revision.
omegas.source: Kernel contest structure + commitment system recognition

omegas.description: If study-as-occupation is correct, when did the revision occur? No formal halakhic moment declared 'study now fulfills sacrifice.' The doctrine emerged gradually, suggesting the authority structure absorbed a functional revision without surfacing it as revision — classic D1 partial drift.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) — no formal revision event

omegas.description: If Temple were rebuilt tomorrow, which reading would the authority structure enforce? Study-as-occupation implies no urgency to resume performance; study-as-archiving implies immediate obligation. Messianic-suspension implies waiting for messianic figure to authorize. The readings predict different responses to the same counterfactual.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) — authority structure benefits from ambiguity

omegas.description: Reform/Reconstructionist readings (sacrifice is obsolete, not suspended) would constitute a fourth reading with explicit revision. Excluded from analysis because they operate outside the rabbinic authority structure that grounds the kernel. But their existence suggests the kernel itself may be contested at a higher level.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium) — analysis assumes Orthodox halakhic framework

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel structure is genuine: three readings share the substrate (Temple sacrifice as binding obligation) but instantiate structurally different constraints (study-as-fulfillment vs study-as-preparation vs study-as-maintenance). The D1/D4 boundary case is documented in omega_d1_d4_boundary.
